simple.meaning: הַדָּם (haddâm) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something stamped to pieces , i.e. a bit.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:5. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הַדָּם (H1917) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: הַדָּם (haddâm) / H1917 is traced through Daniel 2:5, Daniel 3:29 with generated occurrence evidence.

structuredEvidence.definition: something stamped to pieces , i.e. a bit

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king answered the Chaldeans, “The thing has gone from me. If you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut in pieces, and your houses will be made a dunghill.

timeline.evidenceText: The king answered the Chaldeans, “The thing has gone from me. If you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut in pieces, and your houses will be made a dunghill.

Therefore I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill; because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”

definitions.short: something stamped to pieces , i.e. a bit
definitions.full: H1917. haddam [ הַדָּם ] noun [masculine] member, limb (loan-word from Persian , id. Lag Ges. Abh. 28 Fl Levy ChWB i. 423 b ); plural absolute תִּתְעַבְדוּן הַדָּמִין Dan 2:5 ye shall be made members , i.e. dismembered , so 3:29 .
